children: on Thursday announced that an expert panel of the EU drug regulator, the European Medicines Agency (EMA), endorsed Frehemgo, an injectable targeting the bleeding disorder hemophilia A.

EMA’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) issued a positive opinion on Frehemgo, recommending its marketing authorization for use with or without inhibitors, in adults and children with hemophilia A, the company said.

The decision is based on data from the company’s FRONTIER trial program, in which the bispecific antibody outperformed prior clotting factor prophylaxis and on-demand treatments in reducing the annualized bleeding rate in the above patient group.
Subject to the European Commission's approval, the CHMP recommendation paves the way for Novo
to launch Frehemgo in a single-use pre-filled pen for once-monthly, once-every-two-weeks, and once-weekly prophylaxis in hemophilia A.
The Danish drugmaker expects an initial rollout of the drug in a select European country in Q4 2026 before starting an EU-wide launch early next year.

title: Novo hemophilia therapy granted EU recommendation
